raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Resolve the TODO in `verl/trainer/constants_ppo.py` that disables vLLM's compile cache due to vllm-project/vllm#31199. That concurrent cache-write bug was fixed by vllm-project/vllm#35420, first included in vLLM 0.17.0; Torch 2.10+ also contains the native atomic-write fix from pytorch/pytorch#162432. verl now requires vLLM >=0.18.0, so remove the obsolete workaround and restore upstream defaults.

Explicit `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE` values are still forwarded to Ray workers for troubleshooting. The checkpoint server-adapter test also uses upstream defaults. On recent Torch versions, removing this override also restores vLLM's default AOT selection.

No open PR addressing this change was found in the duplicate checks below. This PR does not claim to resolve the separate LoRA issue #3149. AI assistance was used to research and implement this change.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE%22+in%3Abody and https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22compile+cache%22+in%3Atitle
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

- `uv run --no-project --with hydra-core --with pre-commit pre-commit run --files verl/trainer/constants_ppo.py tests/checkpoint_engine/test_special_server_adapter.py --show-diff-on-failure`: all hooks passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

No dedicated tests added for removing the obsolete workaround. The existing checkpoint server-adapter test now exercises default cache behavior when run in GPU CI. GPU tests and startup performance measurements were not run locally.

### API and Usage Example

Leave `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE` unset to use upstream defaults, or set `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` in the launch environment to disable caching.

### Design & Code Changes

Remove the default cache-disable setting and its resolved TODO; preserve explicit overrides in Ray worker environments and remove the same workaround from the existing checkpoint server-adapter test.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Apply repository-wide pre-commit checks: checks were run for both changed files; see the command above.
- [ ] Add / Update documentation: no API changes.
- [ ] Add unit or end-to-end tests: no dedicated tests needed for this workaround removal; the existing GPU test uses default caching.
- [ ] Request CI in the project channel when ready.
- [ ] Update the recipe submodule: not applicable.

@@ -88,9 +88,6 @@ def _uses_torch_profiler(config) -> bool:
         "NCCL_DEBUG": "WARN",
         "VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL": "WARN",
         "VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING": "true",
-        # TODO: disable compile cache due to cache corruption issue
-        # https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31199
-        "VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE": "1",
         # Needed for multi-processes colocated on same NPU device
         # https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/canncommercial/83RC1/maintenref/envvar/envref_07_0143.html
         "HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE": "auto",
@@ -142,6 +139,7 @@ def get_ppo_ray_runtime_env(config=None):
         runtime_env["env_vars"][key] = os.environ.get(key, "0")
     # Forward only when set: empty string breaks vLLM ParallelConfig int parsing.
     for key in (
+        "VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE",
         "PYTHONHASHSEED",
         "CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG",
         "FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC",
